title: Rebuild a Tree From In-Order and Post-Order

concept.title: The post-order ends with the root, so read it from the back
body: This is the previous idea turned around. In the **post-order** list the root is the **last** value (left subtree, right subtree, root). So the post-order list is consumed from the **end**: take the last value as the root, find it in the in-order list, and split the in-order values into the left part and the right part.

The order of the recursive calls changes too. Reading the post-order from the back, you meet the root first, then the values of the **right** subtree (they come just before the root in post-order), then the values of the left subtree. So the **right subtree must be built first**:

body.code:
index = n - 1                                   # the last value of the post-order list

def make(lo, hi):                                # build from inorder[lo..hi]
    global index
    if lo > hi:
        return None
    v = postorder[index]
    index -= 1
    root = TreeNode(v)
    mid = pos[v]
    root.right = make(mid + 1, hi)               # the right subtree first!
    root.left = make(lo, mid - 1)
    return root

body: If you build the left subtree first, the index points into the values of the right subtree and the result is wrong. Getting this order right is the whole difficulty of the problem.

statement: A binary tree has different values. Its in-order list (left subtree, root, right subtree) and its post-order list (left subtree, right subtree, root) are given. Rebuild the tree and print it in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` values in in-order.
The third line has the `n` values in post-order.
outputFormat: The tree in level order on one line.
constraints: -10^9 <= every value <= 10^9, and all values are different
The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The last value of the post-order list is the root 3: 3 9 20 N N 15 7.

hints: The last value of the post-order list is the root.
Split the in-order range at the root.
Walk the post-order list from the end and build the right subtree before the left subtree.

explanation: The post-order list is read from the end: the next value is the root, its place in the in-order list splits the range, and the right part is rebuilt before the left part.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def rebuild(ino, post):
    pos = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(ino)}
    index = [len(post) - 1]

    def make(lo, hi):
        if lo > hi:
            return None
        v = post[index[0]]
        index[0] -= 1
        root = TreeNode(v)
        mid = pos[v]
        root.right = make(mid + 1, hi)
        root.left = make(lo, mid - 1)
        return root

    return make(0, len(ino) - 1)

n = int(input())
ino = list(map(int, input().split()))
post = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_tree(rebuild(ino, post))
